blocks.content:

& 

INFORMATION  NEWS & INFORMATION

Hello, Families!We hope everyone has had a wonderful week! It has been great seeing our students settling into the school year and building new routines. A quick reminder that there will be no school on Monday or Tuesday. We hope your family enjoys the long weekend, and we look forward to welcoming everyone back on Wednesday refreshed and ready to learn.Thank you to everyone who has supported our PTG fundraiser so far. We truly appreciate your generosity and involvement. Your support helps make so many wonderful opportunities possible for our students and staff. Today was also a lot of fun as we had Pajama Day! It was wonderful seeing students and staff dressed in their cozy pajamas while enjoying a day of learning together. Thank you to everyone who participated and helped make it a fun day.Have a safe and relaxing long weekend. We look forward to seeing everyone back at school on Wednesday!Stephanie JonesPrincipal

title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
VOLUNTEER 

& 

VISITOR 

POLICY VOLUNTEER & VISITOR POLICY

As we continue with our volunteer policy this year, please remember that any adult volunteer who wishes to enter the school building must have a volunteer application on file with the office every school year. After a parent’s second visit to the building, they are required to complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office. Please plan to complete this process at least 3 weeks prior to the event. This allows adequate time for the background check to be completed and for the appropriate information to be provided to the school administrator for planning purposes. Once completed, your background check is valid for 5 years.Central Registration Office:Ruth Michael📞 513-273-3101We appreciate your understanding and cooperation as we work to keep our students, staff, and school community safe. Public schools have implemented these regulations to comply with state and federal safety requirements regarding volunteers and visitors in schools.

summary: All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file with the office each school year. After a second visit, parents must complete **fingerprinting and a background check** through the Central Registration Office at least **3 weeks prior** to their event. Background checks are valid for **5 years**. Contact Ruth Michael at **513-273-3101** for Central Registration.

title: Student Cell Phone Policy and Compliance
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Student Cell Phone Usage: Based on compliance with Senate Bill 158 Ohio Senate Bill 158 seeks to promote a focused, respectful learning environment free from personal cell phone distractions during the entirety of the school day.ExpectationsAll student cell phones must be powered off from arrival until dismissal.Phones may be stored in a student backpack and/or cubby and may not be used in classrooms, hallways, restrooms, recess, or the cafeteria at any time during the school day.Additional electronic devices that allow communication or internet use may also be stored should they present a disruption.Consequences for Cell Phone Violations1st Offense - students will receive a warning2nd Offense - phone confiscated & turned into office until the end of the day3rd -Offense - above procedures and the cell phone must be picked up in the office by the parent/guardianSubsequent offenses - progressive discipline, including but not limited to: loss of recess and/or privilegesAll parent/guardian contact must go through the main office. Students are never without access to communication. The school can always connect a student with a guardian using the office phone.School-Wide EmergenciesStudent safety comes first. We will not send students to hallways during an active emergency. Communication with families will be handled centrally by administration, SRO, or district personnel. If students need to access their phones after an emergency to contact family, they will be given permission and time to do so once it is safe. In some situations (e.g., prolonged shelter-in-place or reunification), supervised phone retrieval will be allowed once the situation is stable.Please note, students refusing to comply with an adult’s request to turn their phone in are subject to additional consequences.

summary: **Cell phones must be powered off and stored all day** from arrival to dismissal per Ohio Senate Bill 158. Phones cannot be used in classrooms, hallways, restrooms, recess, or cafeteria. **Violations result in progressive consequences**: 1st offense = warning, 2nd = confiscation until end of day, 3rd = parent pickup required, subsequent = loss of privileges. During school-wide emergencies, students will be given supervised access to phones once safe. All parent contact must go through the main office.

summary: Key dates for the 2026-2027 school year include **no school days** for holidays, professional development, and breaks. **Bookmobile visits** occur monthly throughout the year. Major breaks include **Thanksgiving (Nov 23-27)**, **Winter Break (Dec 21-Jan 1)**, and **Spring Break (Mar 22-26)**. **Parent-teacher conferences** are scheduled for October 8th and 13th from 4:00-7:30 PM. The **last day of school is May 27th, 2027**.
